Analysis of Similarities (ANOSIM)

Source: R/anosim.r
anosim.Rd

Tests whether samples in the same group are more similar to each other than to samples in other groups, from the ranks of the distances between them. Gives the same \(R\) statistic and p-value as vegan::anosim(). Computes them in parallel C, from one ranking of the distances, without the \(n \times n\) matrices that anosim() builds.

Usage

anosim(
  dm,
  groups,
  data = NULL,
  permutations = 999L,
  strata = NULL,
  seed = 0L,
  cpus = n_cpus()
)

Arguments

dm

A dist object, such as from beta_div() or bray(), or a symmetric numeric matrix of distances. Must not contain NAs or negative values.

groups

Each sample's group: a vector or factor with one value per sample, matched to the samples in dm by name when both are named, else in the same order as dm. Or, when data is given, the name of one of its columns (or a vector with one value per row of data). Values are treated as categories, even if they are numbers.

data

Optional sample metadata: a data frame with one row per sample, holding groups (and strata) as columns. Rows are matched to the samples in dm by row name, and rows for other samples are ignored; without row names, they must be in the same order as dm. Default: NULL.

permutations

The number of permutations. Default: 999. Alternatively, a matrix with one permutation of 1:n per row, as from permute::shuffleSet(), to use instead of random ones.

strata

Permute samples only within these groups (blocks), for designs such as repeated measures. With data, the name of one of its columns, or a vector with one value per row of data. Without data, a vector with one value per sample, matched to the samples by name when it has names, otherwise in the same order. Default: NULL (free permutation).

seed

An integer seed for the random permutations. The same seed gives the same p-value. Default: 0

cpus

How many parallel processing threads should be used. The default, n_cpus(), will use all logical CPU cores.

Value

A list of class c("ecodive_anosim", "ecodive_test"), the same shape as the results of ecodive's other permutation tests, with:

  • statistic: The ANOSIM statistic, c(R = ...): vegan::anosim()'s statistic.

  • p_value: Permutation p-value, anosim()'s signif. NA without permutations.

  • z: How many standard deviations \(R\) lies above the mean of the permuted statistics: \((R - mean(R_{perm})) / sd(R_{perm})\), as summary(vegan::permustats()). NA with fewer than two permutations, or when they are all equal.

  • n_perm: The number of permutations.

  • ranks: A data frame with one row for the pairs of samples in different groups ("Between") and one for each group, with the number of pairs and their mean_rank: the averages behind summary(anosim(...))'s quantiles. A group of one sample has no pairs and an NA mean rank.

  • permutation: How samples were permuted: "free", "within strata", or "supplied matrix".

Attribute r_perm is a vector of the \(R\) statistics of each permutation, anosim()'s perm.

Details

Method

ANOSIM (Clarke 1993) ranks all \(M = n(n-1)/2\) distances, from 1 for the smallest to \(M\) for the largest, giving tied distances the average of their ranks. With \(\bar{r}_B\) the mean rank of the distances between samples in different groups, and \(\bar{r}_W\) that of the distances within groups, $$R = \frac{\bar{r}_B - \bar{r}_W}{M / 2}$$ \(R\) is near 0 when the grouping explains nothing, and 1 when every distance within groups is smaller than every distance between them. Negative values mean samples are more alike between groups than within them.

For each permutation, the samples' group labels are shuffled and \(R\) is recomputed. The p-value is the proportion of permutations, counting the observed one, with an \(R\) at least as large: \((1 + \#\{R_{perm} \ge R\}) / (1 + permutations)\). As in anosim(), permuted statistics within sqrt(.Machine$double.eps) of the observed one count as ties.

ANOSIM tests for differences in location, but is also sensitive to differences in spread (dispersion) between groups (Warton et al. 2012); see also permanova().

Speed and memory

The distances are ranked once, with a radix sort. Shuffling the labels doesn't change how many pairs are within groups, nor the sum of all the ranks, so each permutation needs only the sum of the ranks within groups: one pass over the ranks, shared by many permutations at once, with no \(n \times n\) matrix. Permutations run in parallel.

Reproducibility

The permutations come from seed, not from R's random number generator, so set.seed() has no effect, and each permutation has a random number stream of its own. P-values are identical from run to run and for any number of cpus. The random permutations differ from anosim()'s, so p-values agree with it only up to sampling error, unless the same permutations matrix is given to both.

Differences from vegan::anosim()

  • anosim() here takes distances, not a community table: compute them first with beta_div() or a metric function such as bray().

  • The fields are named as in ecodive's other tests: statistic is named R, signif is p_value, and the permuted statistics are attribute r_perm. The full vectors of ranks and their classes (dis.rank and class.vec), each as long as dm, are summarized as the mean rank of each class, in field ranks.

  • strata permutes freely within strata. For other restricted designs, pass a permutations matrix from permute::shuffleSet().

  • When there are fewer possible permutations than requested, vegan (via permute) runs each of them once instead. anosim() always draws random permutations.

  • Negative distances are an error, where vegan warns.

References

Clarke, K. R. (1993). Non-parametric multivariate analyses of changes in community structure. Australian Journal of Ecology, 18(1), 117-143. doi:10.1111/j.1442-9993.1993.tb00438.x

Warton, D. I., Wright, S. T., & Wang, Y. (2012). Distance-based multivariate analyses confound location and dispersion effects. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 3(1), 89-101. doi:10.1111/j.2041-210X.2011.00127.x

See also

permanova(), beta_div()

Examples

    # 30 samples in three treatment groups. The 'high' group has more
    # of the first five genera.
    set.seed(1)
    counts <- matrix(rpois(30 * 20, 5), 30, 20)
    rownames(counts) <- paste0('S', 1:30)
    meta <- data.frame(
      row.names = rownames(counts),
      treatment = rep(c('ctrl', 'low', 'high'), each = 10),
      site      = rep(c('A', 'B'), 15) )
    high <- meta$treatment == 'high'
    counts[high, 1:5] <- counts[high, 1:5] + 5

    dm <- bray(counts)

    # Are samples more alike within treatment groups than between them?
    anosim(dm, 'treatment', meta)
#> Analysis of similarities (ANOSIM)
#> 
#> R = 0.3217, p = 0.001, z = 6.742
#> Permutations: 999 (free)
#> 
#> Mean rank of the distances, between and within groups:
#>         pairs mean_rank
#> Between   300   239.712
#> ctrl       45   221.111
#> high       45    43.500
#> low        45   244.644

    # The same, with the groups as a vector.
    anosim(dm, meta$treatment)
#> Analysis of similarities (ANOSIM)
#> 
#> R = 0.3217, p = 0.001, z = 6.742
#> Permutations: 999 (free)
#> 
#> Mean rank of the distances, between and within groups:
#>         pairs mean_rank
#> Between   300   239.712
#> ctrl       45   221.111
#> high       45    43.500
#> low        45   244.644

    # Permuting treatment labels only within each site.
    anosim(dm, 'treatment', meta, strata = 'site')
#> Analysis of similarities (ANOSIM)
#> 
#> R = 0.3217, p = 0.001, z = 6.714
#> Permutations: 999 (within strata)
#> 
#> Mean rank of the distances, between and within groups:
#>         pairs mean_rank
#> Between   300   239.712
#> ctrl       45   221.111
#> high       45    43.500
#> low        45   244.644

    # Mean rank of the distances between and within groups.
    anosim(dm, 'treatment', meta)$ranks
#>         pairs mean_rank
#> Between   300  239.7117
#> ctrl       45  221.1111
#> high       45   43.5000
#> low        45  244.6444
